stages.name: Rome & Roman Africa
stages.desc: Italy and the Republic's provinces before the civil war, Carthage's old land among them

stages.name: Juba's Numidia
stages.desc: The kingdom of Hiempsal II and his son Juba I, ruled from Cirta

stages.name: Mauretania (Caesarian)
stages.desc: The Moorish kingdoms of Bocchus II and Bogud, Caesar's allies from 49 BC

stages.name: Pompeian-held
stages.desc: Held by Pompey's partisans, their towns and their Numidian ally

stages.name: Caesarian-held
stages.desc: Held by Caesar and the towns that sided with him

stages.name: Annexed in 46 BC
stages.desc: Numidia turned into the Roman province of Africa Nova

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Kingdom of the Mauri beyond the Mulucha river, a friend of Rome
Caesar's party recognises Bocchus II and Bogud as kings and allies
Bocchus is rewarded with Numidian lands to his east

states.name: Libya
timeline: Cyrenaica is a Roman province; Leptis and the Tripolitan ports trade with Rome and Numidia
Cato brings Pompey's defeated men to Cyrene, then west across the Syrtes
Leptis is fined three million pounds of olive oil a year for siding with Juba

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: The province of Africa, Carthage's old land, governed from Utica; the west is Numidian
Pompey's grain command binds the province's harvests and landowners to him
Attius Varus holds Africa for Pompey; Curio's army is destroyed on the Bagradas
Scipio, Cato, Labienus and Juba make Africa the Pompeians' last stronghold
After Thapsus every town submits to Caesar and pays heavy fines

states.name: Italy
timeline: Rome: Julius Caesar, a rising politician deep in debt, is elected Pontifex Maximus
Caesar crosses the Rubicon in January; Pompey and the consuls abandon Italy
Caesar's African triumph parades Juba's small son through Rome

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Numidia of King Hiempsal II, ruled from the rock-top city of Cirta; the far west is Mauretanian
Juba I is king; Curio's bill threatens to confiscate his kingdom
Pompey's senate hails Juba as king; Caesar's party declares him a public enemy
Numidia becomes Africa Nova; Sittius gets Cirta and Bocchus the western lands

events.title: Caesar, chief priest
events.text: Julius Caesar is elected Pontifex Maximus, Rome's chief priest, at thirty-seven.

events.title: Hiempsal's Cirta
events.text: King Hiempsal II, Juba's father, rules Numidia from Cirta as a client of Rome.

events.title: The beard pulled
events.text: Defending the Numidian noble Masintha against King Hiempsal, Caesar seizes young Prince Juba by the beard in open court.

events.title: Masintha smuggled out
events.text: Caesar loses the case, hides Masintha in his house and carries him off in his litter to Spain.

events.title: Caesar's consulship
events.text: Backed by Pompey and Crassus, Caesar holds the consulship and then wins command in Gaul.

events.title: Pompey's grain command
events.text: Rome hands Pompey its grain supply; he tours Sardinia and Africa to bring in the harvest.

events.title: Conference of Luca
events.text: Caesar, Pompey and Crassus renew their alliance at Luca, in Caesar's province.

events.title: Pompey sole consul
events.text: After riots in Rome, Pompey is made sole consul and drifts toward Caesar's enemies.

events.title: King Juba
events.text: By now Juba has succeeded his father as king of Numidia.

events.title: Curio's bill
events.text: The tribune Curio, Caesar's ally, proposes to confiscate Juba's kingdom, making the king his enemy.

events.title: Rubicon crossed
events.text: In January Caesar leads his army into Italy; Pompey and the consuls flee across the Adriatic.

events.title: Varus holds Africa
events.text: Publius Attius Varus seizes the province of Africa for Pompey, and Juba joins him.

events.title: Mauretanian allies
events.text: Caesar's party hails Bocchus II and Bogud as kings and declares Juba a public enemy.

events.title: Curio lands
events.text: Curio crosses from Sicily with two legions and five hundred horsemen.

events.title: Castra Cornelia
events.text: Curio camps on Scipio Africanus's old camp and beats Varus outside Utica.

events.title: Battle of the Bagradas
events.text: On 24 August Juba's general Saburra feigns retreat, then destroys Curio's army; Curio dies fighting.

events.title: Prisoners massacred
events.text: Curio's men who surrender to Varus are put to death on Juba's orders.

events.title: Pharsalus
events.text: Caesar crushes Pompey in Thessaly; Pompey flees to Egypt and is murdered there.

events.title: Cato at Cyrene
events.text: Cyrene opens its gates to Cato, days after shutting them on Labienus.

events.title: March of the Syrtes
events.text: Cato leads the Pompeian survivors west through the desert to Leptis, on foot at their head.

events.title: Scipio in command
events.text: The Pompeian leaders give the supreme command to Metellus Scipio; Cato governs Utica.

events.title: Utica spared
events.text: Juba wants Utica, suspected of favouring Caesar, destroyed; Cato prevents it.

events.title: Caesar lands
events.text: In late December Caesar lands near Hadrumetum with three thousand infantry and 150 horsemen.

events.title: Battle of Ruspina
events.text: On 4 January Labienus and Petreius surround Caesar's small army, which fights its way back to camp.

events.title: Sittius takes Cirta
events.text: The adventurer Publius Sittius and King Bocchus invade Numidia and storm Cirta.

events.title: Juba returns
events.text: Juba rejoins Scipio with three legions, cavalry and thirty elephants.

events.title: Vaga destroyed
events.text: Vaga asks Caesar for a garrison; Juba arrives first and massacres its people.

events.title: Acholla defects
events.text: Coastal towns such as Acholla and Leptis Minor side with Caesar and feed his army.

events.title: Battle of Thapsus
events.text: On 6 April the elephants stampede, the Pompeian army breaks, and Caesar's veterans kill thousands trying to surrender.

events.title: Cato's suicide
events.text: After helping others escape by sea, Cato takes his own life at Utica.

events.title: Utica surrenders
events.text: Utica's Roman merchants are spared but fined two hundred million sesterces.

events.title: Zama shuts its gates
events.text: Juba's royal city, where he built a pyre for his treasure and its people, refuses to let him in.

events.title: Juba and Petreius
events.text: At a country house the two fight a duel to die as soldiers; Juba kills Petreius, then has a slave kill him.

events.title: Scipio's last fleet
events.text: Scipio's ships are caught by Sittius's fleet off Hippo Regius, and Scipio dies by his own hand.

events.title: Africa Nova
events.text: Caesar sells the king's property at Zama and makes Numidia a province, with the historian Sallust as governor.

events.title: Cirta to Sittius
events.text: Sittius's men receive lands around Cirta; Bocchus gains Numidia's west.

events.title: Fines on the towns
events.text: Thapsus and Hadrumetum pay millions of sesterces; Leptis owes three million pounds of oil a year.

events.title: African triumph
events.text: Juba's small son is led in Caesar's triumph; he will grow up to be King Juba II.

metrics.label: Held by Juba and the Pompeians
Held by Caesar and his allies

chartNote: Share of the area of five present-day countries (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Italy), by the power that held most of each. Regions are today's boundaries, and the map is a simplification: ancient Numidia straddled Algeria and Tunisia, Mauretania reached into western Algeria, the Roman province covered only northern Tunisia, the vast desert south was ruled by no one, and many towns took the other side from their region.
